prompt.brief: Design a feature that shows how many users are viewing the same page right now, while remaining useful under reconnects, duplicate tabs, mobile sleep, hot pages, and a large number of concurrent viewers.
successSignals: Define whether the count is exact, approximate, or eventually consistent and show its freshness.
Use expiring leases and idempotent session identities instead of one permanent write per page view.
Separate heartbeat ingestion from count broadcast and keep analytics off the live path.
Plan for hot rooms, reconnect storms, browser sleep, and regional failure explicitly.

functional: Join a page presence room when a page is opened and leave it when the session closes.
Show a count that updates while the page remains open, with a freshness timestamp or stale indicator.
Count one logical session once even if heartbeats are duplicated or retried; optionally merge authenticated tabs by policy.
Handle disconnects, browser sleep, navigation, reconnects, and page deletion safely.
nonFunctional: Keep count updates below 2 seconds under normal load and expire abandoned sessions without client leave events.
Avoid durable per-heartbeat writes; a presence-store failure must not corrupt business data.
Support privacy controls, origin validation, authentication where required, and per-connection quotas.
Degrade to a stale/approximate count rather than blocking page rendering when the live service is unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: 50 million daily active viewers and 5 million concurrent page sessions at peak.
Heartbeats every 15 seconds with a 45-second lease; assume 330K heartbeat messages per second at peak.
Most rooms have fewer than 100 viewers, but the hottest 100 pages can each reach 100K viewers.
Count changes are coalesced for 250ms and analytics samples 1 in 100 presence events.

metrics.label: Heartbeat rate
metrics.description: 5M sessions renewing every 15 seconds; capacity must include reconnect bursts.

metrics.label: Lease window
metrics.description: Three heartbeat intervals tolerate a missed mobile tick while bounding stale presence.

metrics.label: Count freshness
metrics.description: The target for normal live updates; expose stale state when the budget is exceeded.

metrics.label: Hot-room fan-out
metrics.description: Requires coalescing, shard-aware fan-out, and backpressure for popular pages.

entities.name: PresenceSession
entities.notes: Ephemeral session lease for one viewer/page membership.

entities.name: PresenceSnapshot
entities.notes: Coalesced count projection with explicit freshness and approximation.

entities.name: Heartbeat
entities.notes: Sequenced liveness signal used to reject stale reconnects.

apis.notes: Create or resume a session idempotently.
Extend only the current session epoch and reject stale heartbeats.
Return a bounded count with clear stale/degraded semantics.
Subscribe to coalesced count changes with reconnect support.

dataFlow.title: Open a presence session
dataFlow.description: The client obtains a stable session ID and connection epoch; the room router assigns a shard and records a short lease.

dataFlow.title: Refresh liveness
dataFlow.description: Heartbeats extend the lease only when sequence and connection epoch are current; mobile sleep and duplicate tabs remain safe.

dataFlow.title: Expire and count
dataFlow.description: Shard owners remove expired memberships and publish coalesced deltas to a count projector rather than incrementing a global hot key.

dataFlow.title: Broadcast page updates
dataFlow.description: The fanout path sends approximate or exact-enough count updates to subscribed clients with a watermark.

dataFlow.title: Reconnect and repair
dataFlow.description: A reconnect reads the latest snapshot, resumes from a cursor where possible, and repairs shard/count drift asynchronously.

architecture.title: Real-time page presence reference architecture
architecture.summary: Clients send short-lived presence heartbeats; an in-memory membership service owns expiry and publishes a coalesced count to viewers without making every heartbeat a durable database write.

layers.label: Experience layer
layers.description: Browsers join a page presence room and render a freshness-aware count.

layers.label: Presence layer
layers.description: A horizontally scalable connection tier tracks leases and assigns page rooms to shards.

layers.label: Distribution and operations
layers.description: Count changes are coalesced and broadcast; durable analytics remains off the critical path.

keyPaths.label: Join and heartbeat path
keyPaths.description: Client → gateway → presence service → expiring membership store.

keyPaths.label: Count broadcast path
keyPaths.description: Membership change → coalesced count event → fan-out to the page room.

components.label: Page clients
components.description: Open a WebSocket or SSE connection, send a lease heartbeat, and display count plus freshness.

components.label: Edge gateway
components.description: Terminates TLS, authenticates optional users, applies connection and message quotas, and routes by page key.

components.label: Presence service
components.description: Owns join, heartbeat, leave, expiry, room membership, and count coalescing for its assigned shards.

components.label: Room router
components.description: Consistent-hashes page keys so all members of a room meet at the same presence shard.

components.label: Expiring membership store
components.description: Redis-like shard-local state keyed by page and session with TTL leases; it is reconstructable, not the system of record.

properties.expiry: TTL slightly longer than heartbeat interval

components.label: Count change stream
components.description: Buffers compact count updates and lets fan-out scale separately from heartbeat processing.

components.label: Room fan-out
components.description: Publishes the latest coalesced count to connected clients and drops stale sequence numbers.

properties.policy: Coalesce updates over a short window

components.label: Analytics queue
components.description: Receives sampled page-presence events for reporting without coupling analytics to live counts.

components.label: Presence monitoring
components.description: Measures active connections, heartbeat lag, expiry rate, room hot spots, fan-out lag, and count error budget.

connections.label: Connect + heartbeat
connections.description: Open a connection and renew the page lease.

connections.label: Route
connections.description: Validate page identity and route the session to its shard.

connections.label: Lease
connections.description: Add, renew, or remove the session with an expiring key.

connections.label: Count changed
connections.description: Publish only a compact room count after membership changes.

connections.label: Coalesce
connections.description: Deliver the latest count to the fan-out worker.

connections.label: Live count
connections.description: Broadcast count and observed-at timestamp to the page room.

connections.label: Metrics
connections.description: Expose lease, room, shard, and freshness signals.

deepDives.title: Heartbeat leases and reconnect epochs
points: For the real-time page-presence feature, presence is disposable lease state, not a durable user fact, and expired sessions must not count.
Design for the failure case where duplicate tabs, reconnect races, mobile sleep, and hot pages must not create unbounded fanout or phantom viewers; keep retries, versions, and repair state explicit.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

points: For the real-time page-presence feature, presence is disposable lease state, not a durable user fact, and expired sessions must not count.

tradeoffs.title: Exact count versus bounded approximation
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use shard-local membership and coalesced counts; expose approximation and freshness for hot pages.
tradeoffs.caution: A globally exact synchronous counter creates a single hot key and couples every heartbeat to it.

tradeoffs.title: Heartbeat frequency versus battery/load
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use a moderate heartbeat interval, short lease extension, and server-side expiry; tune by device and page value.
tradeoffs.caution: Very frequent heartbeats waste battery and connection capacity; very long leases overcount asleep clients.

tradeoffs.title: Push-only versus snapshot plus deltas
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push coalesced updates but make a snapshot and cursor-based resync authoritative for reconnects.
tradeoffs.caution: Push-only clients drift when mobile networks suspend sockets.

commonMistakes: Counting connections instead of logical sessions.
Letting old reconnect epochs extend a current lease.
Updating one global page counter on every heartbeat.
Treating presence as durable historical identity.
Showing a stale count without timestamp or approximation state.

followUps.question: What if the same user opens three tabs?
followUps.answer: Track session IDs and define product semantics explicitly—count viewers by user or tab—then deduplicate at the room projection.

followUps.question: How do you handle a hot page?
followUps.answer: Shard membership, coalesce updates, cap fanout frequency, and serve a snapshot with approximation metadata.

followUps.question: What if a phone sleeps for ten minutes?
followUps.answer: Let the lease expire, remove membership, and require a new connection epoch on resume.

rubric.description: The answer defines lease-based liveness, duplicate/reconnect handling, hot-room sharding, coalesced fanout, and freshness semantics, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys make the real-time page-presence feature state, versions, lifecycle, and derived projections explicit.
Partitioning, queues, backpressure, cache behavior, hot-key handling, and bounded work are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded behavior, observability, and auditability protect the primary contract.
The candidate can explain the real-time page-presence feature consistency boundary, asynchronous work, and operational limits.
